question.problem: Given the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}9y-3x+6z \\ 3y-x+2z \\ 6x-12z-18y\end{aligned}],$ find $\text{nullity}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 6 \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 6 & -18 & -12\end{aligned}]
$$

Recall that $\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T)).$

In order to find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T)),$ we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 6 \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 6 & -18 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 6 & -18 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has $2$ non-pivot columns (the $2$nd and $3$rd ones). Therefore, 

$$
\text{nullity}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T))=2.
$$
